clue.text: A short time in incredible servitude

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other, as the word 'in' places something within a larger thing

blocks.note: a tall story is one too far-fetched to believe
an hour, written in its short form

explanation.surface: Someone endures a brief but unbelievable spell of slavery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A short time' is not just T: 'short' tells you to abbreviate 'an hour' to HR. THRALL is T(HR)ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in thrall is to be held in bondage, so the noun names the state of slavery itself.

clue.text: One's speechless, as a rule

blocks.note: surface reading: someone who is usually lost for words
setter's reading: silent because a monastic rule forbids talking

explanation.walkthrough: 'As a rule' means usually, but also according to a religious order's rule, which for this Cistercian order includes keeping silence.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of this Cistercian monastic order are known for keeping a vow of silence under their rule.

clue.text: A politician interrupting wild speech that's out of control

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something

blocks.note: a rant is a wild, angry speech
A plus MP, a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An MP heckles during a frenzied tirade that has spiralled out of hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rampant is spreading unchecked, like rampant inflation, so it is unrestrained.

clue.text: Rural road runs round county, one of real wealth

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it

blocks.note: a lane is a country road
the cricket abbreviation for runs
County Down, in Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A country road loops around a county belonging to a rich man.
explanation.walkthrough: LANE plus R surrounds DOWN. 'Real' here means real estate, property in land.
explanation.definitionFit: A landowner holds real property, so their wealth is in real estate rather than money.

clue.text: Class liable to criticise insincere words

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation for class
apt to do something means liable to do it
to rap someone is to rebuke them

explanation.surface: A social group prone to finding fault, which the setter dismisses as empty talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Claptrap is pretentious nonsense spoken to win applause, hence hollow and insincere talk.

clue.text: Minister and nobleman happen to turn up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: a lord is a nobleman
to chance to do something is to happen to
to roll is to turn over

explanation.surface: A government minister and a peer show up by accident.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lord Chancellor is a senior UK government minister, traditionally head of the judiciary.

clue.text: Assume one's in a job

indicators.note: one piece placed in another is held within it

blocks.note: a post is a job
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Taking it for granted that someone is employed.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit is to put forward as a premise, taking something as given for the sake of argument.

clue.text: Check about Italian monk in the chorus

indicators.note: to go about something is to go around it

blocks.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
Fra is the title of an Italian friar

explanation.surface: A monk is restrained while singing in a church choir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check' is itself a meaning of the answer, so it tempts as the definition; but the definition is 'the chorus', and 'Check' is wordplay. Fra is the title given to an Italian friar.
explanation.definitionFit: A refrain is the repeated chorus of a song that recurs after each verse.

clue.text: Conditional release of men locked up in enclosed area

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word reads from bottom to top
being locked in an area means being shut inside it
in places one piece within the other

blocks.note: a pale is a fenced-off area, as in 'beyond the pale'
OR is 'other ranks', soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Prisoners are let out early on terms, having been shut away in a compound.
explanation.definitionFit: Parole is release of a prisoner before the sentence ends, on condition of good behaviour.

clue.text: Belated shock as litigant - he isn't to be represented

indicators.note: to represent is to present again in another form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter, ignoring the dash

explanation.surface: A courtroom twist: someone suing won't have a lawyer after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Represented' suggests legal representation, which fits the litigant, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names an unpleasant surprise coming at the end, like a scorpion's barb.

clue.text: Times building providing services, starting with a carpet

blocks.note: taken as written
the multiplication sign
a minster is a large church where services are held

explanation.surface: Reads like a description of a newspaper office or a church, with floor covering mentioned at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' suggests the newspaper setting the puzzle, but it is just the multiplication sign. 'Starting with a' puts the A at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Axminster is a type of woven pile rug, named after the Devon town where it was first produced.

clue.text: Furniture right, up to this point

blocks.note: a sofa is a piece of furniture
the usual abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A furniture shopper declares everything satisfactory until now.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an everyday idiom meaning until now, as in 'so far, so good'.

clue.text: Unfinished drama shown to performing sections of company

indicators.note: something left unfinished lacks its ending, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: a play is a drama
taken as written
an actor who is on is on stage, performing

explanation.surface: An incomplete play is staged for parts of a theatre company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Company' suggests actors, but here it is a military company, which is divided into platoons.
explanation.definitionFit: A platoon is a subdivision of an army company, so platoons are its sections.

clue.text: Abuse making Tom, for one, cry

blocks.note: a tom is a male cat
a call is a cry

explanation.surface: Someone is so cruelly treated that poor Tom ends up in tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' looks like a person's name; it is a tomcat.
explanation.definitionFit: A catcall is a jeering shout of derision, a form of verbal abuse hurled at a performer or speaker.

clue.text: Pursued an occupation as a dressmaker

definitions.note: loosely, the fabric a dressmaker works with

blocks.note: first meaning, read as two words: staged a sit-in, occupying a building in protest
second meaning: a glossy fabric a dressmaker sews with

explanation.surface: Someone worked in a trade, namely dressmaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occupation' reads as a job, but in the first sense it is the protest kind: to sit in is to occupy premises.
explanation.definitionFit: Protesters who occupy a building sat in; separately, the single word is a smooth glossy cloth used for dresses.

clue.text: People in a state as I had no bananas

indicators.note: going bananas means going crazy, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone frets about being in a state because they had no bananas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a state' sounds like being upset; it really means living in a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Idahoans are residents of Idaho, one of the American states, so they are people living in a state.

clue.text: Exaggerate old distance travelled in Russia to eat out

indicators.note: out suggests something wrong or put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the usual abbreviation for old
a verst is an old Russian measure of distance, about a kilometre
rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone exaggerates how far they travelled in Russia to get to a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: To overstate is to state too strongly, putting something in more extreme terms than are true.

clue.text: Gather to meet new Capone of the underworld

blocks.note: to gather from evidence is to infer
the abbreviation for new
Al Capone, the Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: A gang assembles to meet a fresh Capone, a criminal kingpin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underworld' fits the gangster theme, but the definition means hell, not organised crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Infernal comes from the Latin for the lower regions, so it describes things belonging to hell.

clue.text: Philosopher's follower so politically enlightened, ignoring demo

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out, so that word is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
believing in rule by the people
taken as written, the part removed

explanation.surface: A student of a philosopher is liberal-minded but refuses to join a protest march.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Demo' looks like a protest march in the surface, but it is just the letters to remove from the front of the longer word.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, a Socratic is a disciple of Socrates, the Athenian thinker, so a philosopher's adherent.

clue.text: Unjustly treat pair captured by misbehaving posse

indicators.note: something captured is held inside its captor
misbehaving means not keeping in line, so these letters fall out of order

blocks.note: the letters of posse, rearranged
the abbreviation for pair

explanation.surface: A rowdy sheriff's posse catches two people and mistreats them.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppress is to keep people down by cruel or unfair use of power.

clue.text: Half-hearted trivial complaint rejected in Scottish town

indicators.note: losing half its heart means one of the two middle letters is dropped
something rejected is sent back, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: a niggle is a petty grumble

explanation.surface: A feeble grumble is turned down somewhere in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: NIGGLE has a double G at its heart; removing one leaves NIGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Elgin is a cathedral town in Moray, in the north-east of Scotland.

clue.text: Making jokes, but getting silence

blocks.note: first meaning: telling gags, as a comedian does
second meaning: silencing someone, putting a gag on them

explanation.surface: A comedian tells jokes but the audience stays silent.
explanation.definitionFit: A gag is both a joke and something stuffed in a mouth to stop speech, so the verb has both senses.

clue.text: Computer circuit finally doesn't work

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word that follows

blocks.note: a lap is one circuit of a track
the last letter of doesn't
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A computer's circuitry has given up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doesn't work' reads as a breakdown, but 'work' gives OP and 'doesn't' gives only its end letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A laptop is a portable personal computer small enough to use on one's lap.

clue.text: Inform of an award in speech

indicators.note: in speech means as it is pronounced, so we go by the sound, not the spelling

blocks.note: an award is a prize; said quickly, the two words run together

explanation.surface: Someone is told, perhaps in an address, about a prize being given.
explanation.definitionFit: To apprise someone of something is to tell them about it, a formal synonym for notify.

clue.text: Leaders of it nurture democracy in Asia

definitions.text: Leaders of it nurture democracy in Asia

indicators.note: the leaders of a group of words are their first letters

blocks.note: the opening letters of these five words

explanation.surface: A country's leaders foster democracy in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the country famously the world's largest democracy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Asian nation is the largest democracy on earth, so its rulers are fostering democracy there.

clue.text: Getting Italian meal, sink is in the way

indicators.note: one word sits inside the other, as 'is in' places something within

blocks.note: a lane is a way or road
to sag is to sink down

explanation.surface: While making pasta, the kitchen sink gets in the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagne is a baked Italian dish of layered flat pasta sheets with sauce and cheese.

clue.text: Put one's foot down to get student, finally, to study

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word before it

blocks.note: the last letter of student
to read a subject at university is to study it

explanation.surface: A firm teacher insists that a pupil finally gets down to some study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put one's foot down' suggests being firm; here it is literal, a step. To read a subject is the British way of saying you study it at university.
explanation.definitionFit: To tread is literally to step, placing a foot on the ground.

clue.text: Love to act, getting into a part

indicators.note: getting into something means going inside it

blocks.note: A plus RATION, a ration being a share or portion
to do is to act

explanation.surface: An actor loves performing and landing a role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part' looks like a stage role, but it means a portion or ration.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is deep love or worship, so the noun is a strong synonym for devoted affection.

clue.text: Allowing one across is barely adequate

blocks.note: first meaning: able to be crossed or travelled through, as of a road
second meaning: just about acceptable, so-so

explanation.surface: A crossing that lets someone through only just does its job.
explanation.definitionFit: A road that can be traversed is fit for travel; a performance that merely scrapes by is only just acceptable.

clue.text: Girl standing on mountain in part of Asia

indicators.note: in an across clue, standing on something means coming after it, as if resting on top of it

blocks.note: ben is a Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis
an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: A young woman poses atop a peak somewhere in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standing on' puts the girl after the mountain in this across clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Bengal is a region of the Indian subcontinent, now divided between India and Bangladesh.
